questions.prompt: A blocker bluff works better when you hold…

choices.text: A card that removes the nuts from their calling range, such as the ace of the flush suit when you do not have a flush.
A card that blocks their folds
No blockers and no pair, chosen at random
The board pair, which you then fold

questions.explanation: Block the hands that call, not the hands that fold.

questions.prompt: Bluffing a calling station is usually…

choices.text: A mistake. They call with the hands you needed to fold.

questions.explanation: Bluffs need folds. Stations do not fold. Value-bet them instead.

choices.text: Polarized spots: the nuts or a selected bluff, not a medium pair.

questions.explanation: A huge size represents a very strong hand. Medium strength should not use it.

choices.text: The cards you hold are the ones they would have folded, so more of those folds are still in the deck for them.
You hold the ace of their flush

questions.explanation: Good bluffs block calls and leave their folds in the deck. Holding a hand they fold removes a bluff candidate from them and is the wrong blocker.
